cards.text: God is still speaking to Moses, Israel's leader, giving him the plans for the tabernacle and its priests (Exodus 25-29). Now He adds one more altar, made of acacia wood.

cards.question: This acacia wood altar gets one special job. What is it for?

cards.text: It's small and square, with horns, covered in pure gold, with gold-covered poles to carry it. It goes in front of the veil, before the ark of the Testimony and the mercy seat. Every morning when Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), tends the lamps, he burns fragrant incense on it, and again at twilight when he sets them up. No snooze button for Aaron.

cards.question: God tells Moses what that spot in front of the veil, before the mercy seat, will be. What does He say?

answers.text: It's where God will meet with Moses
It's where the elders will gather
It's where the people will bring gifts

cards.question: God says the incense on this altar is to burn before the LORD for the generations to come.

cards.text: God also says what must never go on this altar, starting with any unauthorized incense.

cards.question: Aaron can offer a burnt offering on the incense altar.

cards.text: Once a year, for all the generations to come, Aaron makes atonement on the horns of this altar. God says, "The altar is most holy to the LORD."

Then the LORD gives Moses rules for a census, a count of the Israelites. Each man twenty or older who is counted pays the LORD a ransom for his life. Rich or poor, it's the same half shekel. Friend, I spent years in the back of the Millers' junk drawer, and NOBODY in that kitchen ever counted me.

cards.question: God tells Moses what will happen when each counted man pays the ransom for his life. What does He say?

answers.text: No plague will come on them
Their names will be kept forever

cards.question: God tells Moses what to do with the census money. What is it for?

answers.text: The service of the Tent of Meeting
Gifts for the poor in Israel

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Moses to make a bronze basin on a bronze stand. It goes between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, filled with water.

cards.question: What is the water in the bronze basin for?

cards.text: Aaron and his sons wash their hands and feet there whenever they go into the Tent of Meeting or come up to the altar to present a food offering. Every kitchen knows that move, friend: hands under the water BEFORE anybody touches the dough.

cards.question: God gives a serious reason why the priests must wash at the basin. What is it?

answers.text: So that they will not die
So that the people will trust them
So that the altar will stay clean

cards.text: Next, God gives Moses a formula with the finest spices: liquid myrrh, cinnamon, fragrant cane and cassia, weighed out by the shekel, plus a hin of olive oil.

cards.question: What does Moses make from all those fine spices?

cards.text: With it, Moses is to anoint the Tent of Meeting, the ark and every furnishing with its utensils, right down to the basin and its stand.

cards.question: God says anything that touches these anointed things shall be holy.
Besides the Tent of Meeting and its furnishings, who does Moses anoint with this oil?

cards.text: Then God gives Moses a message for the Israelites: this will be His sacred anointing oil for the generations to come.

cards.question: An Israelite may make oil with the same formula for his own use.
What happens to anyone who mixes perfume like the sacred oil or puts it on an outsider?

answers.text: He is cut off from his people
He pays a fine of a half shekel
He washes in the basin seven days

cards.text: Last, God gives Moses a formula for incense: gum resin, onycha, galbanum and pure frankincense in equal measures, blended by a perfumer and seasoned with salt. Equal measures, friend, no eyeballing it, and believe me, I have eyeballed a LOT of chocolate chips.
Some of it is ground into fine powder and placed in front of the Testimony in the Tent of Meeting. God says, "It shall be most holy to you."

cards.question: An Israelite may make this incense at home just to enjoy how it smells.

cards.text: That's where we'll leave it for now, friend. God isn't finished giving Moses His instructions.
